newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS-Dlr/yen, dlr/mark vols weaken with spot.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-Dlr/yen, dlr/mark vols weaken with spot.

text.p: Dlr/yen and dollar/mark implied options volatilities declined slightly in very quiet trade as spot retreated from its recent highs, traders said.
They said the dollar was consolidating after recent volatility.
"They seem to be a little softer at the moment, volatilities are off from yesterday and there's not an awful lot of stuff trading," one options trader said.
"It seems to have calmed down as Greenspan speaks to the Senate," she said.
Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan delivered testimony to the Senate Finance Committee Thursday morning, but many currency traders noted he did not discuss current economic conditions.
One-month dollar/mark vols were trading at 10.4/10.6 at midmorning, down from 10.6/10.8 near the open, said a trader with an overseas bank.
One-month dollar/yen traded midmorning at 12.3/12.6 versus 12.4/12.7 earlier in the day, he said.
Several traders noted muted options activity.
The bank trader noted that vols, while off slightly, were not as soft as one might expect.
"Risk reversals clearly favor the dollar upside and there's good demand for options out there," he said.

"Volatilities aren't that much easier, particularly in dollar/yen," he said. "There's a lot of nervousness in that currency but so long as the dollar doesn't collapse you could see vols come off only slightly," he said.
An IMM currency options trader agreed that action so far Thursday was very quiet as the market came away with little direction from Greenspan's testimony.

"It just in general is taking a breather," said Alan Revercomb, options strategist for I.D.E.A. "Vols have gone from nine percent to 13 percent in the yen during the course of last week and this week," he said. "You've had a big rise, but it hasn't been unjustified," he said.
He put support in one-month dollar/yen at 11.0 percent.
He said the market was likely waiting for U.S gross domestic product data due on Friday. Fourth-quarter advance real GDP was forecast up 3.9 percent versus 2.1 percent in the previous report.
